facts.text: Opportunity Rover was deployed at Meridiani Planum during Opportunity (MER-B) in 2004.

Opportunity landed on 25 January 2004 for a 90-sol mission and operated for nearly 15 years — over 55 times its planned lifetime. It drove 45.16 km across the Martian surface, the longest distance travelled by any off-Earth wheeled vehicle. A planet-wide dust storm in June 2018 blocked sunlight to its solar panels. Last contact: 10 June 2018.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Provided the first ground-truth evidence that Mars once had sustained surface water, through haematite concretions and water-laid sedimentary rock at Meridiani Planum.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Meridiani Planum.
Opportunity rests in Perseverance Valley on Endeavour Crater's rim, silent since the June 2018 global dust storm; NASA declared it lost on 13 February 2019.
